notes_and_textual_formulas.text: Notes:
Both buy and sell positions have been considered
Options Value (Buy/Sell) = Strike price * Qty
Futures Value (Buy/Sell) = Traded Price * Qty
Value & Open Interest at the end of day:
Options Value (End of day) = Underlying Close Price * Qty
Futures Value (End of day) = Closing Futures Price * Qty  (closing price is the daily settlement price of futures contracts)

files.formula_caveat: Stored values only; no native Excel rendering or recalculation performed

source.document_title: NSDL : Fortnightly Sector-wise FII Investment data
source.provenance_caveat: NSDL title, saved CDSL URL, and localhost form action coexist; this is an archived local report, not independently fetched current data.

main_table.period_value_note: AUC is a stock, fortnightly net investment is a flow; their difference is not an ownership-percent change.

reconciliation.fx_caveat: Reported inputs are rounded whole INR crore / USD million; these comparisons describe stored report arithmetic, not a currency-quality threshold.

notes: Note: The net investment and AUC of FPIs in Debt VRR segment have been included in the aforesaid report w.e.f. April 30, 2020.
The AUC of FPIs in Debt-FAR, Mutual Funds and AIF segment have been included in the aforesaid report w.e.f. August 31, 2024.
The Net investment of FPIs in Debt-FAR, Mutual Funds and AIF segment have been included in the aforesaid report w.e.f. September 15, 2024.

Note: BSE and NSE vide its Press release dated March 21, 2022 have informed and adopted Common Industry Classification structure for Companies Listed and Traded at NSE and BSE. Accordingly, NSDL has considered the aforesaid new Common Industry Classification structure as provided by BSE in respect of aforesaid report w.e.f. April 30, 2022. For Sector classification, please refer to BSE industry classification as published on its website : https://www.bseindia.com/static/about/Industry_Classification.aspx BSE has classified around 4800 number of issuers into 22 sectors. NSDL has decided to rely on the BSE classification. Any FPI investment outside those 4800 issuers, is classified under 'Others'.
fx_table: Note: RBI reference rate is used for conversion from INR to USD

INR to USD conversion of FPI net Investment details on NSDL website is done on the basis of daily RBI reference rate. However here RBI reference rate of end of period is used for conversion fromINR to USD.
